item.title: Roundcube University Espionage, BeyondTrust Auth Bypasses, and Tenda CVE-2026-11405 Backdoor
item.content:encoded:
Suspected China-Aligned Hackers Exploit Roundcube Flaws Against Universities — Must Read

A suspected China-aligned group tracked as UNK_MassTraction is exploiting patched Roundcube webmail flaws at U.S. and Canadian university physics and engineering departments to steal credentials and gain persistent access to mail servers. The campaign uses an XSS-to-RCE chain with IceCube, SquareShell, VShell, and SNOWLIGHT, showing that exposed mail servers should be defended like other edge devices.

  • Proofpoint observed a suspected China-aligned activity cluster, tracked as UNK_MassTraction, exploiting Roundcube webmail software used by physics and engineering departments at U.S. and Canadian universities.
  • The campaign targets administrators and professors in departments with national security ties or research areas including astrophysics and particle physics.
  • The attackers exploit patched Roundcube flaws including CVE-2024-42009 to steal credentials, two-factor authentication data, and cookies, then use CVE-2025-49113 to attempt remote code execution on the mail server.
  • After exploitation, the campaign can deploy a web shell called SquareShell or the post-exploitation tool VShell, with a fallback chain involving a shell script and the SNOWLIGHT ELF loader.
  • Proofpoint said the campaign shows that email delivery can enable compromise of mail servers and that Chinese operators are treating mail servers like other externally exposed network devices.

BeyondTrust warns of critical flaws in remote access software — Must Read

BeyondTrust patched critical authentication-bypass flaws in its Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access products that could let unauthenticated attackers access vulnerable appliances under specific configurations. Cloud customers are already patched, while self-hosted customers should apply the April security rollup or upgrade to version 25.3.3 or later.

  • BeyondTrust warned customers to patch two critical flaws in Remote Support versions 25.3.2 or earlier and Privileged Remote Access versions 25.3.2 or earlier that could allow authentication bypass.
  • CVE-2026-40138 can let attackers without privileges bypass access controls and access targeted appliances, including accounts with elevated privileges, under a specific enabled authentication configuration.
  • CVE-2026-40139 stems from improper processing of BeyondTrust Remote Support authentication requests and can let unauthenticated remote attackers gain unauthorized access to vulnerable instances.
  • BeyondTrust also patched CVE-2026-40140 and CVE-2026-40141, two high-severity issues that can be used to cause denial of service or access restricted resources on unpatched Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access instances.
  • BeyondTrust said all Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access cloud customers were patched as of April 21, 2026, while self-hosted customers should apply the April security rollup or upgrade to version 25.3.3 or later.

CERT/CC Warns of Hidden Admin Backdoor in Tenda Router Firmware — Should Read

CERT/CC warns that several Tenda router firmware versions contain an undocumented admin backdoor that can bypass normal password checks and grant full web-management control. No patch is available yet, so users should disable remote management and reduce device exposure.

  • CERT/CC warned that several Tenda firmware versions contain an undocumented authentication backdoor that enables administrative access to the devices' web management interfaces.
  • The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-11405 and can allow an attacker to bypass password verification and obtain full administrative control without valid credentials.
  • The backdoor is present in the login() function of the /bin/httpd web server binary and uses an alternate password value stored as sys.rzadmin.password when normal authentication fails.
  • CERT/CC said the associated rzadmin username is not validated, so any username can succeed if paired with the backdoor password.
  • The vulnerability remained unpatched at the time of writing, and users were advised to disable remote management and change the default LAN IP address.

Microsoft testing new Cloud Rebuild Windows 11 recovery feature — May Read

Microsoft is testing a new Windows 11 Cloud Rebuild recovery feature that can reinstall Windows from the cloud, including drivers, even when a PC will not boot. The feature is aimed at helping users and administrators restore broken or inoperable systems without USB media or relying on the existing OS installation.

  • Microsoft has begun testing the Cloud Rebuild recovery feature in the latest Windows 11 Insider Preview builds for users in the Experimental channel.
  • Cloud Rebuild can remotely trigger a complete Windows 11 system reinstall from the cloud for devices with persistent problems or that have become inoperable.
  • Microsoft says Cloud Rebuild downloads both the target Windows image and the device's drivers from Windows Update, so recovery does not require USB media, a custom image, or a healthy existing operating system.
  • Windows Insiders can test Cloud Rebuild after installing Windows 11 Insider Experimental Preview Build 26300.8772 and selecting the Cloud rebuild option in the Windows Recovery Environment under Troubleshoot and Recovery.
  • Cloud Rebuild is part of Microsoft's Windows Resiliency Initiative, alongside Point-in-Time Restore and Quick Machine Recovery features intended to help restore devices that cannot start or function properly.

Microsoft to enable Windows settings backup by default for orgs — May Read

Microsoft will enable Windows settings backup by default on eligible Microsoft Entra-joined enterprise devices after upgrading to Windows 11 26H2, unless admins explicitly disable it. Restore will still require admin configuration, and the change excludes DMA-regulated regions and restricted cloud environments.

  • Microsoft says the Windows settings backup and restore tool will be enabled by default on Microsoft Entra-joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid-joined enterprise systems after upgrading to Windows 11 26H2.
  • The backup tool, formerly known as Windows Backup for Organizations, helps enterprise users back up and restore Windows settings after a device is reset, replaced, upgraded, or reimaged.
  • The default-on behavior will apply only to eligible devices where administrators have not explicitly configured the backup policy, and explicit enablement or disablement settings will be honored.
  • Windows backup default-on behavior will not apply to devices in countries or regions regulated by the EU Digital Markets Act, sovereign or restricted cloud environments, or systems where the backup policy is already configured.
  • Restore behavior will not be enabled by default, and users will need explicit administrator configuration to restore Windows devices.

Why CISOs are the Architects of Yes — Optional

CISOs are under pressure to enable rapid AI adoption, but spending more on AI security is not translating into confidence because real-time governance and controls are still lacking. The key takeaway is that CISOs should act as “architects of yes” by building discovery, data protection, identity, and governance frameworks that let the business use AI safely.

  • The article argues that CISOs are facing pressure from boards and CEOs to enable AI adoption across organizations rather than simply block new tools.
  • It cites BCG research saying 72% of CEOs are the main decision makers on AI in their organizations, twice as many as a year ago.
  • Netskope research cited in the article found that 90% of cybersecurity professionals increased their AI security budgets this year, while 29% feel less secure than they did twelve months ago.
  • The article says AI is deployed in 73% of organizations, but only 7% have governance that enforces security policy in real time.
  • The author says a defensible “yes” to AI requires discovery of AI use, data-layer controls, identity for agents, governance for AI, agents and MCP, and adaptive monitoring.

Capitalize on Mythos Hype to Fix Your Exposure and Vulnerability Management — Optional

The article argues that hype around AI-driven exploit tools should push organizations to fix longstanding exposure management gaps by prioritizing vulnerabilities based on real exploitability, reachability, and business impact rather than static severity scores. XM Cyber promotes continuous attack-path validation and choke-point remediation as a way to reduce risk faster with less wasted effort.

  • The article says hype around Anthropic’s Claude Mythos Preview, OpenAI GPT-5.5-cyber, and autonomous attackers has moved cyber risk discussions into executive and board conversations.
  • The article cites Gartner as saying only 48% of organizations prioritize exposures based on likelihood and business impact, leaving many business-critical assets exposed for longer.
  • The article says highly exploitable vulnerabilities take an average of 134 days to remediate because most organizations do not use exploitability factors to prioritize fixes.
  • The article argues that static CVSS scoring and isolated vulnerability lists fail because they ignore whether a flaw is reachable or exploitable in a specific environment.
  • The article presents XM Cyber’s Continuous Exposure Management platform as a way to map attack paths, identify choke points, and focus remediation on exposures that affect mission-critical assets.

The Security Loop: Continuously Improving Preemptive Defense — Optional

Silent Push promotes its “Security Loop” approach, where each alert or suspicious indicator is used to map related infrastructure, improve detections, block threats, and feed lessons back into defenses. The key takeaway is that security teams should turn investigations into a continuous cycle of preemptive improvement rather than one-off reactive responses.

  • The Security Loop is presented as a way for security teams to move from isolated, reactive investigations to a continuously improving preemptive defense process.
  • Every alert, suspicious domain, IP, or incident is treated as a starting point in the Security Loop.
  • Security teams use Silent Push to map related infrastructure, understand wider threat context, create better detections, block connected infrastructure, and feed the learning back into the security stack.
  • The Security Loop is described as working through detection, contextualization, hunting, response, prevention, learning, and repetition.
  • The article says security improves with every cycle rather than resetting after every incident.

Using Preemptive Cyber Defense Data in AI Agents and Workflows — Optional

Silent Push is promoting how AI agents can use preemptive cyber defense data to enrich indicators, uncover related attacker infrastructure, and feed SOAR/SIEM workflows. The key takeaway is that security teams can move from reacting to single alerts toward proactively tracking emerging threat infrastructure before it becomes active.

  • The video explains how AI agents can support preemptive cyber defense workflows by helping security teams move from single alerts to wider infrastructure clusters.
  • Silent Push Senior Solutions Engineer Nick Roy explores how teams can enrich indicators and identify related domains.
  • The video covers feeding intelligence into SOAR and SIEM workflows.
  • The video describes building watch lists for emerging attacker infrastructure before it becomes active.
  • Silent Push says AI agents and its platform can help make threat hunting faster, more scalable, and more proactive.

Silent Push and NYSE Discuss Preemptive Cyber Defense — Optional

Silent Push is promoting its preemptive defense approach, which analyzes attacker infrastructure to identify indicators of future attack before threats are launched. The company says this lets security teams proactively block malicious domains, IPs, and DNS records before they are weaponized.

  • Silent Push recently sat down with NYSE to discuss the differences between traditional threat intelligence and preemptive defense.
  • Silent Push says it analyzes how adversaries build and manage their infrastructure to create digital fingerprints of attacker behavior.
  • Silent Push says this process generates Indicators of Future Attack, described as proactive domains, IPs, and DNS records that identify adversary intent before an attack is launched.
  • Silent Push says its approach helps security teams proactively block hidden threats before they are weaponized.
  • The article invites readers to book a demo of Silent Push.
